findings.impact: The bilingual example can teach sister as specifically an older sister even though the English supplies no age relationship.
findings.evidence: Snapshot lines 190–191: Asked whom he trusted, he unhesitatingly named his sister. is translated with 自分の姉. The sibling definition at https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/sister does not distinguish older from younger. The manner adverb and the rest of the pair are sound.
findings.action: Make the pair agree by adding older before sister in the original English, or use Japanese that does not specify relative age. No change to the unhesitatingly definition or score is needed.

coverage_notes: The two main meanings are proportionate: ease/availability with explicit promptness, and willingness/no hesitation. Dictionary differences in splitting promptness do not require a third block here.

All requested areas and all examples were inspected. Common adjective/participle modification, modal/perfect and postverbal placement, negation and comparison, recall, physical change, acceptance and admission are covered. No material missing modern sense or construction was established.

The displayed common Oxford US/UK pronunciation and Middle English ready-plus-ly history are supported. Other dictionaries show legitimate schwa or final-vowel transcription variants; these do not invalidate the chosen form. No audio was auditioned.
Readiness is correctly identified as a related noun based on ready, not directly derived from readily. A core image is appropriately omitted for two numbered senses.

The selected comparisons and negative-scope guidance are sound aside from the one local translation finding. Scores are per-defined-sense global-English editorial bands; no corpus measurement or unsupported numerical replacement is claimed.
